title: Doping-driven evolution of pairing symmetry in pressurized La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$
authors: Hai-Yang Zhang, Yu-Jie Bai, Fan-Jie Kong
abstract: We investigate the superconducting pairing symmetry and its doping evolution in pressurized La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$. For the undoped compound, the most favorable pairing state is found to be $s_{\pm}$-wave, characterized by sign reversal of the gap functions between the Fermi pockets. A detailed analysis of the pairing interactions reveals that this unconventional state originates from repulsive interactions mediated by the magnetic odd modes of the bilayer nickelate. Upon hole doping, the $γ$ Fermi pocket expands, which amplifies the intrapocket repulsions on this pocket. These repulsions, driven by the magnetic even modes, gradually dominates the pairing interactions and ultimately drive a transition in pairing symmetry from $s_{\pm}$-wave to $d_{xy}$-wave in the heavily hole-doped regime. In stark contrast, the $s_{\pm}$-wave pairing persists under electron doping, even deep into the heavily electron-doped regime where a Lifshitz transition occurs. This finding suggests that the $γ$ Fermi pocket is not essential for the emergence of superconductivity in bilayer nickelates. In fact, the $s_{\pm}$-wave pairing becomes more robust in the absence of the $γ$ pocket, as spin fluctuations are strongly enhanced by the favorable nesting between the $α$ and $β$ pockets --- a condition guaranteed by Luttinger's theorem and the Fermi surface topology. We believe that exploring the doping evolution of superconducting pairing will open a new realm for testing the pairing mechanism in pressurized La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$.
summary: This theoretical study maps the doping-driven evolution of superconductivity in pressurized La3Ni2O7 using a bilayer two-orbital model. It finds that while hole doping induces a symmetry change to $d_{xy}$-wave, electron doping maintains $s_{\pm}$-wave pairing. Crucially, the research concludes that the $\gamma$ Fermi pocket is not essential for superconductivity, suggesting robust pairing driven by $\alpha- eta$ nesting.
main_problem: The study investigates how the superconducting pairing symmetry evolves as a function of doping in the pressurized bilayer nickelate superconductor, La3Ni2O7.
main_result: Hole doping drives a transition from $s_{\pm}$-wave to $d_{xy}$-wave pairing, while electron doping maintains $s_{\pm}$-wave pairing, suggesting the $\gamma$ pocket is not essential for superconductivity.
method: The pairing interaction is calculated using the Random-Phase Approximation (RPA) applied to a minimal bilayer-two-orbital Hamiltonian, utilizing spin and charge susceptibilities.
model_or_system: The system is pressurized La3Ni2O7, modeled by a minimal bilayer-two-orbital Hamiltonian including hopping integrals and onsite interactions. The analysis tracks the superconducting pairing symmetry across different doping levels (hole vs. electron doping).
key_observables: Superconducting pairing symmetry ($s_{\pm}$-wave, $d_{xy}$-wave), gap function sign reversal, and the doping dependence of pairing interactions ($\Gamma_{\alpha eta}, \Gamma_{ eta\gamma}, \Gamma_{\gamma\gamma}$).
important_parameters: Doping level (hole vs. electron), magnetic excitation modes (odd vs. even), and the presence/absence of the $\gamma$ Fermi pocket.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Random-Phase Approximation (RPA) applied to the minimal bilayer-two-orbital model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the leading pairing states at different doping levels, showing the $	heta$-dependence of pairing interactions and the resulting gap distributions for both hole- and electron-doped regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the pairing interaction using RPA, first establishing the $s_{\pm}$-wave state in the undoped limit via magnetic odd modes. It then examines the doping dependence, showing the $s_{\pm} 	o d_{xy}$ transition upon hole doping, and the persistence of $s_{\pm}$ pairing in the electron-doped regime, arguing against the necessity of the $\gamma$ pocket.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical mechanism linking Fermi surface topology (pocket expansion/contraction) and magnetic fluctuations (odd/even modes) to the specific symmetry of the superconducting pairing, which is a core topic in strongly correlated electron physics.
